title: DEMONSTRATION / behavior test — qualitative education

units_of_analysis: Tutor accounts and situated feedback episodes in adult literacy teaching
phenomena_or_topics: Tutors’ descriptions of adapting feedback for learners using multiple languages
relationships_or_questions: What do tutors count as feedback and adaptation in adult literacy learning?
How do tutors explain language choice, timing, modality and directness of feedback?
What tensions or constraints do tutors describe, and what discrepant accounts occur?
How do program setting, tutor experience and language repertoire shape the transferability of accounts?
contexts: Community, voluntary and formal adult literacy provision; retain tutor training and learner language context
geographic_scope: No geographic restriction proposed; compare institutional and language-policy settings
scope.temporal_scope: No publication-year restriction proposed; record fieldwork dates and program changes
languages: Proposed initial English screening; other languages flagged for human translation decision
source_types: Original qualitative interview, focus-group, observational and reflective accounts with tutor voice identifiable

subquestions: What do tutors count as feedback and adaptation in adult literacy learning?
How do tutors explain language choice, timing, modality and directness of feedback?
What tensions or constraints do tutors describe, and what discrepant accounts occur?
How do program setting, tutor experience and language repertoire shape the transferability of accounts?

concept_definitions.definition: Paid or volunteer educators supporting adult reading and writing; not school-age teachers unless adult provision is separable
concept_definitions.label: adult literacy tutors

concept_definitions.definition: Responses to learner work or understanding adjusted in language, timing, modality or interaction; exclude generic differentiation with no feedback episode
concept_definitions.label: adaptive feedback

concept_definitions.definition: Adults using or learning across multiple languages; do not presume migration status or treat multilingualism as a deficit
concept_definitions.label: multilingual learners

include: Original qualitative material about tutors in adult literacy provision describing feedback adaptations for multilingual learners
Mixed-method studies only for separately identifiable qualitative tutor accounts
Learner or observational material may contextualize tutor accounts but must remain attributed to its own perspective
exclude: School-child-only teaching or higher-education disciplinary writing without adult literacy provision
Learner-only accounts with no tutor description relevant to the question
Quantitative effectiveness scores without qualitative accounts; generic multilingual pedagogy with no feedback adaptation

strategy_groups: Combine adult-literacy educator terms with feedback terms; use multilingual terminology as an additional family to avoid assuming all authors use the same label
Plan reference tracing and program terminology expansion after discovery; do not require a qualitative-method label in every query
